title: Away to the South, part 3
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: The Scarecrow was thinking again, and his head bulged out so horribly that Dorothy feared it would burst.
“Let us call in the soldier with the green whiskers,” he said, “and ask his advice.”
So the soldier was summoned and entered the Throne Room timidly, for while Oz was alive he never was allowed to come farther than the door.
“This little girl,” said the Scarecrow to the soldier, “wishes to cross the desert. How can she do so?”
“I cannot tell,” answered the soldier, “for nobody has ever crossed the desert, unless it is Oz himself.”
“Is there no one who can help me?” asked Dorothy earnestly.
“The Witch of the South. She is the most powerful of all the Witches, and rules over the Quadlings. Besides, her castle stands on the edge of the desert, so she may know a way to cross it.”
“Glinda is a Good Witch, isn’t she?” asked the child.

“The Quadlings think she is good,” said the soldier, “and she is kind to everyone. I have heard that Glinda is a beautiful woman, who knows how to keep young in spite of the many years she has lived.”
“How can I get to her castle?” asked Dorothy.

“The road is straight to the South,” he answered, “but it is said to be full of dangers to travelers. There are wild beasts in the woods, and a race of queer men who do not like strangers to cross their country. For this reason none of the Quadlings ever come to the Emerald City.”
The soldier then left them and the Scarecrow said:

“It seems, in spite of dangers, that the best thing Dorothy can do is to travel to the Land of the South and ask Glinda to help her. For, of course, if Dorothy stays here she will never get back to Kansas.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whom does the soldier name as a possible helper?
options: Glinda
Gayelette
The Queen of the Field Mice
The Guardian of the Gates

questions.prompt: Per the passage, who is Glinda?
options: The Witch of the South, who rules the Quadlings
The Witch of the North, who kissed Dorothy
A sorceress who lives in a ruby palace
The wife of the Wizard of Oz

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does Glinda's castle stand?
options: On the edge of the desert
In the middle of a great forest
Beside the Emerald City wall
On an island in a river

questions.prompt: Per the passage, which way does the road to Glinda run?
options: Straight to the South
Straight to the North
East, towards the rising sun
West, into the Winkie country

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why had the soldier never come past the door before?
options: Oz had never allowed it while he was alive
He was too frightened of the great Head
The Guardian of the Gates forbade it
He had only just joined the Palace guard

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what has the soldier heard about Glinda?
options: That she is beautiful and keeps young despite her years
That she has never been seen by any living person
That she is more wicked than the Witch of the West
That she once ruled the Emerald City herself

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what makes the southern road dangerous?
options: Wild beasts in the woods and men who dislike strangers
A desert that must be crossed twice over
The Winged Monkeys, who patrol that country
A river too deep and swift to ford

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why do no Quadlings visit the Emerald City?
options: The road between is full of dangers
They are forbidden by Glinda
They have never heard of the city
The desert lies between them

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does summoned mean?
options: Sent for
Dismissed
Questioned
Rewarded

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A new name and a dangerous road become Dorothy's only chance
A soldier proves that the desert cannot be crossed at all
The Scarecrow decides Dorothy must stay in the city
Glinda arrives at the Emerald City to help them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who does the soldier say has crossed the desert?
options: Nobody, unless it is Oz himself
Glinda and her Quadlings
The Winged Monkeys, many times
The Wicked Witch of the West

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how is Glinda described as treating people?
options: She is kind to everyone
She is feared by all the Quadlings
She sees nobody but her own people
She demands payment for her help

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how powerful is Glinda said to be?
options: The most powerful of all the Witches
Less powerful than the Witch of the North
About equal to the Wizard of Oz
Powerful only within her own castle

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did Dorothy fear about the Scarecrow's head?
options: That it would burst, it bulged so horribly
That the pins would fall out of it
That the brains had stopped working
That he would think himself too clever

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the Scarecrow's argument for going south?
options: Staying in the city means never getting back to Kansas
Glinda has already promised to help her
The dangers of the road have been exaggerated
The Quadlings will give them fresh supplies

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does timidly describe about the soldier?
options: He came in nervously
He came in proudly
He came in quickly
He came in unwillingly

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A soldier's advice turns the journey south, dangers and all
A soldier proves that Dorothy can never leave Oz
The Scarecrow decides to send the Lion instead
Glinda is revealed to be a wicked witch after all
